items.title: The Options Market Says Adobe Stock Can Fall Over A Third Or Rise More Than Half
items.summary: Adobe has deliberately traded near-term recurring revenue for free users, and the option chain is charging for the uncertainty that leaves behind.

items.title: Intel Stock Drops After $15 Billion Share Sale. Is AI Spending Getting Too Expensive?
items.summary: Intel just chose to sell $15 billion worth of its own stock rather than borrow more money, and shareholders are already paying the price. The question hanging over the entire AI infrastructure boom is whether anyone building it will ever generate enough cash to justify the cost.

items.title: CoreWeave Stock Rallied Ahead Of Its Own Numbers, Not On Them
items.summary: The only fresh operating news of the week does not come online for another two years.

items.title: Semis Surge, Michael Burry’s Shorts Feel the Pressure — But Don’t Expect Him to Run for Cover After His Latest “1987-Style” Crash Warning
items.summary: Michael Burry just doubled down on his bearish AI bets even as semiconductors roar back, but one short in his portfolio stands out as a head-scratcher that may reveal a flaw in his entire thesis.

items.title: Salesforce Declines 17% Over the Past Year: How to Play CRM Stock?
items.summary: Salesforce's 17% drop reflects broader software pressure, but resilient growth, rising AI ARR and a lower valuation offer reasons to hold CRM.

items.title: Nvidia investing up to $3 billion in Lancium for Stargate
items.summary: The deal values Lancium, which owns the first operational Stargate site in Abilene, Texas, at around $10 billion

items.title: Oracle’s Rebound Is All But Assured So I Keep Buying
items.summary: Oracle shares have shed a third of their value since last December, yet something in the company's latest earnings report has one investor hitting the buy button harder than ever before.

items.title: 1 Software Stock to Own for Decades and 2 We Question
items.summary: Software is eating the world, and virtually no business is left untouched by it. The undeniable tailwinds fueling the industry have also led to strong returns for SaaS stocks lately as they’ve gained 30.3% over the past six months, outpacing the S&P 500’s 10.9% rise.
